title: Keep the faith: Nisperos rediscovers confidence after yearlong PVL injury layoff
summary: Once one of the Philippines’ biggest names in high school and college volleyball, Akari star Faith Nisperos now fights to stay healthy and finally unlock her true potential in the PVL

blocks.text: BACK IN FORM. Akari star Faith Nisperos celebrates a play in PVL action.
MIX GATPANDAN/RAPPLER
Once one of the Philippines’ biggest names in high school and college volleyball, Akari star Faith Nisperos now fights to stay healthy and finally unlock her true potential in the PVL
MANILA, Philippines – For years, Faith Nisperos was a name thrown around in numerous conversations as one of Philippine volleyball’s brightest future stars.

From her time in high school with the dynastic Nazareth-NU Lady Bullpups, to her stint with the Ateneo Blue Eagles in college, and finally, to her jump to the pros with the PVL’s Akari Chargers, Nisperos always had hype surrounding her, and lived up to it for the most part.

In recent times, however, Ateneo’s former “Queen Eagle” had quietly faded into the volleyball landscape’s backdrop, grounded and clipped by a major knee injury that kept her sidelined from April 2024 until July this year.

Save from a brief and scoreless one-game appearance last January 31, Nisperos sat out more or less 15 months’ worth of a budding volleyball career, before finally shaking off her injury tag for good at the start of the 2026 PVL On Tour, and played every game since then.

The 26-year-old spiker then marked the end of a breakthrough 2026 with a 15-point winning effort — her highest scoring mark since November 2024 — in what was otherwise a no-bearing game against ZUS Coffee last November 17.

Though Akari failed to make the playoffs for the 2026 All-Filipino Conference Siklab Series, Nisperos nonetheless felt like a champion after ending the year on a winning and, more importantly, healthy note.

“I’m really happy because I’m finally here. This is me, and this is my territory,” she said in Filipino. “I have to also give credit to my coaches and my teammates who are beside me throughout my process of going back into the game.”

Despite only playing one to two sets at a time due to the Siklab Series’ “all-to-play” requirement, Nisperos still averaged a respectable 6.5 points per game, and played in all of Akari’s eight elimination round matches that netted a 3-5 record.

Though restrictions were in place, Nisperos did not downplay the difficulty of both finding her confidence back, and striving for consistency amid the ever-present dangers of reaggravating her injury.

“It has been months of mental preparation, because I knew that I would return to form one day, I just didn’t know when,” she continued. “Part of the mental preparation was us getting back under pressure again, going through so much scrutiny, and so much responsibilities.”

“I also had people who helped me throughout that mental process. Again, I go back to my coaches and teammates, who also reminded me that I got this. ‘You’re Faith, remember that. You’re strong,’ they said. They always reminded me who I really am.”

Heading into 2027 for the next two All-Filipino Conferences, Sigla and Sinag, Nisperos is raring to further rediscover her true, peak form — the Faith Nisperos that once won V-League MVP in college and led Ateneo to the Final Four as the main star.

“It’s a common denominator for us athletes that we want to get better as time proceeds,” she continued. “I feel like I just want to be more consistent, and improve my non-scoring skills like receiving and defense.”
“Improvement is always one of my biggest goals as a player. I’ve wanted that for such a long time, to improve myself further.”
Stars who faded into obscurity due to injuries are a dime a dozen in all sports. Nisperos could have gone that route, and could very well still go that route, if her fortunes don’t hold.

After all, she’s never had the best of luck. Prior to her yearlong injury spell, Nisperos also lost two more years of her career after her college rookie season was cut short due to the onset of the 2020 pandemic.
But she’s not holding herself to what-ifs stemming from a rocky past.
True to her name, Nisperos always kept the faith — faith in the process, in her potential, and in the light of a future that she fought hard to keep bright. – Rappler.com
